title: WHAT IF YOU COULD SWITCH OFF SLEEP?

segments.line: Here's the catch. The switch turns off feeling tired.
It doesn't turn off being tired.
When you sleep, the gaps between your brain cells open up, and fluid washes out the day's waste.
In mice, those gaps grow by about sixty percent. That's real.
No sleep, no wash. The waste just… stays.
And after about a day awake, your reactions test about as badly as someone too drunk to legally drive. That's real too.
Your hands shake when you pour cereal.
Words on the page slide around. You keep reading the same line.
And the whole time, you feel fine. That's the scary part.
The longest anyone's ever been watched staying awake on purpose? About eleven days.
Then your phone rings. Unknown number.
Someone's heard about a kid who never sleeps.
